title: God

questions.text: What is the nature of God?
Who are the three persons of the Trinity?
How does God regard human beings?
Does God care about our problems?

applications.text: Love God with all my heart

decision: I believe in God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. I promise to love and obey Him as my Heavenly Father.

additional.title: Introduction
paragraphs: We believe in one God. (1 Corinthians 8:6) Revealed in three persons. (Matthew 28:19) Creator of the universe. (Genesis 1:1; Isaiah 45:18; Hebrews 1:10)

What is God like? He is immortal. (1 Timothy 6:16) He is spirit. (John 4:24) He is eternal. (Isaiah 57:15) He is unchanging. (James 1:17) He is perfect. (Matthew 5:48) He is wise. (1 Corinthians 1:24) He is holy. (Exodus 15:11) He is truth. (Jeremiah 10:10) He is merciful. (Psalms 86:15)
Ways God reveals Himself: Through nature. (Psalms 19:1) Through the Bible. (Revelation 1:1) Through the Lord Jesus. (John 14:6)
God is our Father: He cares about our problems. (Psalms 46:1) He bears with us in mercy. (Jeremiah 31:3) He comforts us in sorrow. (2 Corinthians 1:3) He provides what we lack. (Philippians 4:19)

Our attitude toward God: We should trust Him. (Psalms 52:8) Keep His commandments. (Ecclesiastes 12:13) If we obey Him, things will work for our good. (Romans 8:28) God is always willing to receive us. (James 4:8)

additional.title: Our need for God
paragraphs: The reason for the misfortunes and sufferings that people endure is their departure from God. The prophet Jeremiah speaks of how terrible this mistake is: “For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, to dig for themselves broken cisterns that hold no water.” (Jeremiah 2:13)

The only solution is to return to God. Dr. Andrew Conway Ivy, a renowned professor at the University of Illinois, said: “Believing in God provides the only, the most complete, essential, and rational meaning to existence.” Philosopher Will Durant adds: “The great problem of our time is not communism against individualism; nor Europe against America; nor even East against West. It is whether humanity can bear to live without God.” The wonderful thing is that as soon as we take a step toward God, we will find Him waiting for us with love and mercy.

additional.title: The existence of God
paragraphs: Some say: I do not believe in God because I cannot see Him. Yet we believe in many things we cannot see, such as electricity, wind, and love. Others say: I do not believe because I do not understand God. An unbelieving scholar walked along a beach, thinking about how to understand God. Suddenly he saw a child using a seashell to take water from the sea and empty it into a hole in the sand.
“I want to empty the sea into this hole,” the child said.
“Ah!” the scholar said to himself. “That is what I am trying to do: faced with the ocean of the infinite, I want to pour it all into my finite mind.”

Who does not believe in God? “The fool has said in his heart: There is no God.” (Psalms 14:1) What do scientists say about God? Sir Isaac Newton, the famous discoverer of the law of universal gravitation, said: “The admirable order of the sun, planets, and comets could only have come from the plan and direction of an omniscient and omnipotent being. It follows that God is indeed a divine, wise, and almighty God, a being above everything and infinitely higher than the human mind. We arrive at the suggestion that God must be thought of as the sum of all the powers of the universe.” As Sir Francis Bacon said: “A little science inclines the human spirit toward atheism, but philosophical depths lead human spirits toward religion.”

additional.title: Trust in God
paragraphs: Dr. Werner Von Braun, father of interplanetary rockets, said: “Our need for God is based solely on admiration and awe. People need faith just as they need food, water, and air.”

The Bible contains wonderful promises for those who trust God. “All things work together for good for those who love God.” (Romans 8:28) “If God is for us, who can be against us?” (Romans 8:31) God comforts us in all our troubles. (2 Corinthians 1:6,7) God can supply all our needs. (Philippians 4:19) He is our ready help in trouble. (Psalms 46:1) All things are possible with God. (Matthew 19:26) We can trust in God’s mercy forever. (Psalms 52:8)

What should we do so that God will be with us and protect us? Long for God with all our heart. (Psalms 42:1) Obey God and keep His commandments. (Ecclesiastes 12:13) We cannot serve both God and the world. (Matthew 6:24) Put God above everything. (Matthew 6:33) Love Him with all our heart. (Matthew 22:37) Felix of Nola, a devoted Christian, was fleeing his enemies through the mountains. He came to a cave and took refuge there. A spider spun a web across the entrance. Seeing the web, his pursuers passed by. Felix then said: “Where God is, a spider’s web is a wall; where He is absent, a wall is only a spider’s web.”

Lincoln was very worried. A minister told him: Do not worry, sir, God is on our side. The president replied: I am less concerned about knowing whether He is on our side than about knowing for certain that we are on God’s side.
